paper_title: It Is Easy to Be Wise After the Event: Communicating Finite-State Machines Capture First-Order Logic with "Happened Before"
classifications: Theory of computation → Logic and verification
statement: We leave open whether there is a one-dimensional temporal logic over MSCs, with a finite set of FO-definable modalities, that is expressively complete for FO[→, C, ≤].
context: Since (bounded) MSCs can be seen as a special case of Mazurkiewicz traces [9], we also get Zielonka’s theorem [33] (though a weaker, nondeterministic version, and without guarantee on the size of the constructed automaton). We leave open whether there is a one-dimensional temporal logic over MSCs, with a finite set of FO-definable modalities, that is expressively complete for FO[→, C, ≤].
